Subject: Post-call: Acme AI competitive TCO follow-up & next tests

Hi Simon — thanks again for the time today. Quick recap and proposed next steps based on our discovery: 

Summary of what we heard:
- Primary workload: real-time chat assistant for support agents (avg prompt+response tokens ~ 1,200; 85% of sessions are under 2k tokens)
- Target latency: p95 < 350ms for 1–2 concurrent user queries per agent
- Current usage: ~250k queries/month, planning to scale to ~2M queries/month in Q3
- Key evaluation asks: cost/TCO vs hyperscaler endpoints, latency under production concurrency, and cache/batching impact on unit economics

What we’ll deliver to help you evaluate: 
1) A simple cost model (attached) that lays out per-1M token unit economics across typical configurations (hosted Redwood vs hyperscaler-managed endpoint vs self-hosted on k8s). It includes assumptions for batching, cache hit rate, and sequence length.
2) Benchmark instructions and a small harness to run a performance pass from your environment / our dedicated test runner (see attached).
3) Proposed test matrix: a) baseline single-request latency (no batching), b) batching at 8/16, c) prefix/KV cache enabled to estimate hit-rate improvements (we recommend testing at your realistic cache-hit targets: 10%, 30%, 60%).

Immediate asks for you: 
- Can you confirm the average and P95 sequence lengths you saw in production logs? (we used ~1.2k avg in the model)
- Do you have a preferred 2-hour window next week for us to run a controlled perf pass from your test environment (we can also run from our Dedicated pool if you prefer)?

Attachments: [Attachment: redwood_cost_model_v1.xlsx (xlsx, 72 KB)], [Attachment: benchmark_instructions.md (text, 8 KB)]

Thanks — happy to jump on another quick call to walk through the spreadsheet.

Best,

From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Post-call: Acme AI competitive TCO follow-up & next tests

Hey Simon — thanks for the details. Two quick clarifications and a sketch of numbers you can use right away (see caveats below).

Assumptions I used for the quick model:
- Average sequence length: 1,200 tokens (prompt+response)
- Batch sizes: single (no batching), 8, 16
- Cache hit rate scenarios: 10%, 30%, 60%
- Tokenization consistent with standard BPE; costs expressed per 1M tokens processed (in/out counted)
- Latency targets assume a low-concurrency perf environment; production p95 will be higher depending on concurrent users

Illustrative unit economics (examples; final numbers in attached spreadsheet):
- Redwood Hosted (optimized runtime, auto-batching, KV cache, prefix reuse):
  - No cache, batching=1: ~$12 per 1M tokens
  - Cache hit 30%, batching effective=8: ~$6.50 per 1M tokens
  - Cache hit 60%, batching effective=16: ~$3.80 per 1M tokens

- Hyperscaler X managed endpoint (standard):
  - No cache, batching=1: ~$18 per 1M tokens (includes managed infra/overhead)
  - Cache hit 30%, batching=8: ~$11 per 1M tokens

- Self-hosted (on-prem GPUs w/ ops overhead):
  - Effective cost depends heavily on utilization; at 70% utilization we model ~$9–$14 per 1M tokens (capex amortized)

Notes & caveats:
- These are illustrative; final TCO depends on your actual concurrency profile, retention of KV cache, and model quantization choices.
- Autoscaling overhead: we included a buffer for ephemeral scale-ups (~10% on top of steady-state cost) in the hosted and hyperscaler numbers. If you expect frequent spikes, we can model a higher buffer.
- Batching efficiency: the numbers assume batching is achievable for a significant portion of traffic; for interactive UI traffic you should expect a smaller effective batch size and thus higher per-token cost.

Next steps I recommend:
1) Let us run the perf harness in your proposed window (2026-03-17 14:00–16:00 PDT). We’ll run the three scenarios (no batching, batching=8, batching=16) and report back p95/p99 latencies, throughput, and observed cache hit rates.
2) We’ll populate the spreadsheet with measured numbers and produce a conservative/optimistic TCO view.
3) If the numbers look good, we can provision a short Dedicated trial for more realistic concurrency tests.

If you want, I can also include a simple per-minute burn chart that shows savings as cache-hit increases (helps procurement see upside).

Cheers,
Marcus Lin
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
marcus.lin@redwood.com
